It's like there's no point to the day before it's even started.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself feeling guilty or worthless, or are these feelings of sadness and emptiness more about a lack of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: Honestly, I feel both of those deeply. I constantly feel worthless and replay tiny mistakes from work, like using the wrong toner a year ago, convinced I've ruined everyone's life just by existing. At the same time, I feel completely blank and empty, and I can't even bring myself to care about talking to my mom or seeing my friends anymore.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when these feelings of guilt and worthlessness started, and if they seem to be triggered by specific events or if they're more constant?\n\nPatient: They started a little over a year ago when the pressure at the salon really began piling up, and now they feel pretty constant. They get especially intense when I replay tiny mistakes, like using the wrong toner last year, which makes me feel like I don't deserve my job or friends and have ruined everyone's life just by existing.\n\nDoctor: Was there a specific traumatic or extremely stressful event that occurred around the time these feelings started, or has it been more of a gradual buildup of stress and pressure?\n\nPatient: It was definitely more of a gradual buildup of stress rather than one single event. Transitioning from cosmetology school to working full-time at a busy salon with back-to-back bookings and financial strain slowly wore me down. Over several months, those pressures just piled up until my routines completely fell apart.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the pressures at work and financial strain as significant factors, but can you tell me if there was ever a point where you experienced an intense, overwhelming event or situation that seemed to mark a turning point in how you felt, even if it was part of a gradual buildup?\n\nPatient: The turning point was when I showed up late to work several times in one month and had a complete breakdown in the salon's back room, crying because I couldn't trust my own mind anymore. My supervisor got really concerned about my decline in focus and urged me to see a professional. That was when I finally realized how bad things had truly gotten.\n\nDoctor: Did the feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and sadness start immediately after the breakdown in the salon's back room, or were they present before but intensified after that event?\n\nPatient: Those feelings of sadness, guilt, and emptiness were definitely present long before that breakdown. I had already been carrying that heavy gray cloud for over a year as the work pressure piled up. The breakdown in the back room was just the breaking point where I completely lost control and felt like I couldn't trust my own mind anymore.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the breakdown in the salon's back room seemed to trigger a significant worsening of your symptoms, or did it mainly serve as a realization of how severe your struggles had become?\n\nPatient: It was definitely more of a realization and a breaking point rather than a trigger for new symptoms. I had already been struggling with my focus, memory, and other symptoms for a long time before that day. That breakdown was just the moment where the decline became too hard to hide, and I finally had to admit out loud that I couldn't trust my own mind anymore.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a gradual buildup of stress and pressures at work, but can you tell me if there was a specific period where your symptoms seemed to intensify or change significantly, possibly marking a shift from one set of feelings to another, such as from feeling overwhelmed to feeling persistently sad and empty?\n\nPatient: Yes, there was a definite shift. For the first few months after starting full-time at the salon about two years ago, I was mostly just stressed and trying my best to cope. But about a year and a few months ago, the pressure became too much to carry, and that overwhelm turned into this constant, heavy feeling of sadness and emptiness that never goes away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this constant, heavy feeling of sadness and emptiness, and if it has been present every day since it started, or if there have been any periods where you felt somewhat better?\n\nPatient: I’ve felt this heavy, empty feeling almost every single day for a little over a year now, and I can't recall more than a few brief weeks where I didn't feel deeply down. There was a brief stretch last fall where the crushing sadness lifted slightly and I could get through my shifts a bit better. However, even during that time, I still kept hearing that man's voice behind me and worrying that my coworkers were secretly recording me.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long the periods where you felt somewhat better lasted, and did those periods meet the criteria of at least two months without significant depressive symptoms?\n\nPatient: The times when I felt a little better only lasted for a few brief weeks at most, so they definitely never reached two months. For the vast majority of the last year and a half, I have felt deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day with very little relief.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods lasting at least two months where you did not have significant depressive symptoms, such as feelings of sadness, emptiness, or guilt, over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any long stretches like two months without those feelings. Looking back over this whole period, I can only recall a few brief weeks at a time when I didn't feel deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you've had any periods lasting at least two months without significant depressive symptoms, such as feeling sad, empty, or guilty, at any point over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: No, I can definitely confirm that I haven't had any periods lasting two months without those feelings. Ever since things got bad at the salon, the longest I've gone without feeling deeply down, empty, or guilty is only a few brief weeks at a time.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you've experienced persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and guilt for more than two years now, with brief periods of slight improvement but never a full two months without significant symptoms, is that correct?\n\nPatient: Not exactly—while my overall struggles and decline started almost two years ago when I transitioned to full-time work, the heavy, constant feelings of sadness, emptiness, and guilt have been present for a little over a year. During this past year, I have only had brief periods of a few weeks at most where I felt slightly better, and I definitely haven't had a full two months free of those symptoms.\n\nDoctor: To summarize, you've had a persistent depressive state for over a year with no periods of two months or more without significant symptoms, but can you clarify if there were any distinct episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks but less than two months within this timeframe?\n\nPatient: It hasn't really felt like separate, distinct episodes for me. Instead, it’s just been one continuous, heavy, and empty feeling for over a year now, and I can't recall more than a few brief weeks at a time where I didn't feel deeply down.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any periods of significant improvement, where you felt like your normal self for at least a couple of weeks, before returning to these feelings of sadness and emptiness over the past year?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods where I felt like my normal self. Over the past year or so, I have felt deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day. Even during that brief stretch last fall when the heavy sadness lifted slightly and I could manage my shifts a bit better, I still didn't feel like myself because I was still hearing that man's voice and believing my coworkers were recording me.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any distinct periods of at least two weeks where your depressive symptoms, such as feeling sad, empty, or guilty, were significantly worse than they are now, or has it been a more constant level of severity over the past year?\n\nPatient: It has been a very constant, steady presence for a little over a year now rather than having distinct periods of being significantly worse. It has felt consistently heavy and draining almost every single day, with only those few brief weeks where I felt slightly better. The severity has just stayed pretty much the same throughout.\n\nDoctor: You've described a continuous feeling of sadness and emptiness for over a year with brief periods of slight improvement, but can you confirm if you've ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt completely back to your normal self before returning to these depressive feelings?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had a period where I felt completely back to my normal self. Even during those few brief weeks where the sadness wasn't quite as heavy, I still didn't feel like myself, and those empty feelings have been there almost constantly for over a year now.\n\nDoctor: To clarify the duration of your depressive symptoms, can you confirm if you have experienced a continuous period of depressive symptoms lasting at least two years, or if there have been any periods of significant improvement that lasted for a few months?\n\nPatient: No, the heavy, empty feelings have been going on for a little over a year now, rather than a full two years, and I've never had improvements that lasted for months. I can't really remember more than a few brief weeks at a time when I didn't feel down or guilty. Even during a stretch last fall when I didn't feel quite as crushingly sad and could get through work a bit better, that man's voice and the feeling of being recorded still persisted.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you've had these persistent depressive symptoms for more than a year now without any periods of full recovery or normal functioning that lasted for at least two months, is that correct?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's exactly right. I've felt consistently low and empty for a little over a year now, and I can't remember having any periods of normal functioning or full recovery that lasted more than a few brief weeks at a time.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of significant depressive symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks but less than two months, or has it been a continuous feeling of sadness and emptiness for the entire year?"

Over several months, those pressures just piled up until my routines completely fell apart.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the pressures at work and financial strain as significant factors, but can you tell me if there was ever a point where you experienced an intense, overwhelming event or situation that seemed to mark a turning point in how you felt, even if it was part of a gradual buildup?\n\nPatient: The turning point was when I showed up late to work several times in one month and had a complete breakdown in the salon's back room, crying because I couldn't trust my own mind anymore. My supervisor got really concerned about my decline in focus and urged me to see a professional. That was when I finally realized how bad things had truly gotten.\n\nDoctor: Did the feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and sadness start immediately after the breakdown in the salon's back room, or were they present before but intensified after that event?\n\nPatient: Those feelings of sadness, guilt, and emptiness were definitely present long before that breakdown. I had already been carrying that heavy gray cloud for over a year as the work pressure piled up. The breakdown in the back room was just the breaking point where I completely lost control and felt like I couldn't trust my own mind anymore.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the breakdown in the salon's back room seemed to trigger a significant worsening of your symptoms, or did it mainly serve as a realization of how severe your struggles had become?\n\nPatient: It was definitely more of a realization and a breaking point rather than a trigger for new symptoms. I had already been struggling with my focus, memory, and other symptoms for a long time before that day. That breakdown was just the moment where the decline became too hard to hide, and I finally had to admit out loud that I couldn't trust my own mind anymore.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a gradual buildup of stress and pressures at work, but can you tell me if there was a specific period where your symptoms seemed to intensify or change significantly, possibly marking a shift from one set of feelings to another, such as from feeling overwhelmed to feeling persistently sad and empty?\n\nPatient: Yes, there was a definite shift. For the first few months after starting full-time at the salon about two years ago, I was mostly just stressed and trying my best to cope. But about a year and a few months ago, the pressure became too much to carry, and that overwhelm turned into this constant, heavy feeling of sadness and emptiness that never goes away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this constant, heavy feeling of sadness and emptiness, and if it has been present every day since it started, or if there have been any periods where you felt somewhat better?\n\nPatient: I’ve felt this heavy, empty feeling almost every single day for a little over a year now, and I can't recall more than a few brief weeks where I didn't feel deeply down. There was a brief stretch last fall where the crushing sadness lifted slightly and I could get through my shifts a bit better. However, even during that time, I still kept hearing that man's voice behind me and worrying that my coworkers were secretly recording me.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long the periods where you felt somewhat better lasted, and did those periods meet the criteria of at least two months without significant depressive symptoms?\n\nPatient: The times when I felt a little better only lasted for a few brief weeks at most, so they definitely never reached two months. For the vast majority of the last year and a half, I have felt deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day with very little relief.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods lasting at least two months where you did not have significant depressive symptoms, such as feelings of sadness, emptiness, or guilt, over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any long stretches like two months without those feelings. Looking back over this whole period, I can only recall a few brief weeks at a time when I didn't feel deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you've had any periods lasting at least two months without significant depressive symptoms, such as feeling sad, empty, or guilty, at any point over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: No, I can definitely confirm that I haven't had any periods lasting two months without those feelings. Ever since things got bad at the salon, the longest I've gone without feeling deeply down, empty, or guilty is only a few brief weeks at a time.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you've experienced persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and guilt for more than two years now, with brief periods of slight improvement but never a full two months without significant symptoms, is that correct?\n\nPatient: Not exactly—while my overall struggles and decline started almost two years ago when I transitioned to full-time work, the heavy, constant feelings of sadness, emptiness, and guilt have been present for a little over a year. During this past year, I have only had brief periods of a few weeks at most where I felt slightly better, and I definitely haven't had a full two months free of those symptoms.\n\nDoctor: To summarize, you've had a persistent depressive state for over a year with no periods of two months or more without significant symptoms, but can you clarify if there were any distinct episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks but less than two months within this timeframe?\n\nPatient: It hasn't really felt like separate, distinct episodes for me. Instead, it’s just been one continuous, heavy, and empty feeling for over a year now, and I can't recall more than a few brief weeks at a time where I didn't feel deeply down.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any periods of significant improvement, where you felt like your normal self for at least a couple of weeks, before returning to these feelings of sadness and emptiness over the past year?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods where I felt like my normal self. Over the past year or so, I have felt deeply down, empty, and guilty almost every single day.
